Name: Amanda Rowe
Badge: Teacher as Researcher | Sustaining Literacy Routines
Looking back on this inquiry cycle, what did you learn about your teaching and your students that you might not have noticed otherwise? How did engaging in this teacher-research process shape or shift your thinking about your classroom practice?:

Students as well as myself, was more willing to try this method because I knew what would be expected of me. I think my students could say the same. Overall I was really hesitant because I lack confidence in my writing abilities. I had a total of 14 students with only 3 of those students being 8th graders while the rest were 7th graders. I think the 8th graders had some confidence in their writing due to being a grade higher and more experience, however I think this benefited my 7th graders to see and how much effort they were willing to put forth towards each task asked of them. I LOVED the layering piece, because I think it allowed students to build from where they were and then gain some confidence. Since everyone had the same resources I also think that did level the playing field and students knew they had good information as opposed to worrying about is my resource reliable.

Think back to a moment during the lesson sequence that stands out. It could be a comment from a student, an unexpected challenge or success, a shift in engagement, or a moment when your own thinking changed. Describe what happened and why this moment feels meaningful to you now. What does it reveal:
During the visual representation portion I got lots of different responses. Some students took this idea, ran with it and made their own thinking in a visual. Others really struggled with it and just wanted to write words or sentences from texts because that seemed like the safe option.
As you look over the drafts your students produced in this lesson sequence, what early patterns, surprises, or questions are emerging for you? What aspects of your students’ writing are you most curious to explore more deeply with colleagues during our April regroup? What, if any, questions do you h:
My hesitation in the writing process may not have hindered me helping students the best that I could have. I did the work along side the students to have examples to reference, however I think an English teacher would produce more confident student work.
